web.description:
[Close](https://nairametrics.com/2026/07/16/nigerian-startups-top-10-attract-132-2-million-capture-71-funding-in-h1-2026/)

![Nigerian startups: Top 10 attract $132.2 million, capture 71% funding in H1 2026](https://cdn.nairametrics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Startup-Nigeria-From-Unsplash--scaled.jpeg)

Nigeria’s startup ecosystem recorded a strong first half of 2026, with 51 startups attracting a combined $184.7 million in disclosed funding between January and June.

#### **What the data is saying**
- Funding increased to $184.7 million across 51 deals in H1 2026, representing a 3.59% year-on-year increase in funding value, even as deal volume declined by about 19%.

#### **10. Tuteria — $2.6 million**
The Nigerian education technology startup secured $2.6 million in a venture round in January 2026, backed by Enza Capital and Chui Ventures. The funding is expected to support the company’s expansion, strengthen its technology platform, and widen access to its marketplace that connects learners with verified tutors across Nigeria.

#### **More Insights**
For the Sector breakdown, Fintech remained the leading hub of Nigeria’s startup ecosystem during H1 2026.

The sector attracted $98.5 million, accounting for 53.33% of total funding across 21 deals, reflecting sustained investor confidence in payments, digital banking, embedded finance, lending and cross-border financial services.

- Seed funding contributed $17.7 million (9.58%), while pre-seed rounds raised $9.5 million (5.14%). Pre-seed extensions added another $1 million, while grants contributed $0.2 million.

#### **What this means**
The H1 2026 data shows a slightly stronger but more selective funding market for Nigerian startups.

web.title: Nigeria reclaims Africa’s startup funding lead as investments ...
web.description:
[Close](https://nairametrics.com/2026/10/21/nigeria-reclaims-africas-startup-funding-lead-as-investments-rise-to-635-million/)

![Nigeria reclaims Africa’s startup funding lead as investments rise to $635 million](https://cdn.nairametrics.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Media-25.webp)

Nigeria reclaimed its position as Africa’s leading destination for startup funding in the first nine months of 2026, attracting $635 million, more than double the amount recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

The country also recorded the highest number of startups raising at least $100,000, with 77 ventures securing funding during the period, up 10% from 70 in the first nine months of 2025. Excluding pan-African ventures, Nigeria accounted for 37% of startup funding raised by country-specific ventures across the continent, its highest share since 2021.

#### **Moove, Flutterwave lead major funding rounds**
- Moove, the mobility financing company, which earlier this month [announced plans to exit Nigeria](https://nairametrics.com/2026/10/08/moove-exits-nigeria-gives-customers-n35-billion-worth-of-cars/), raised $250 million, while fintech company Flutterwave secured $100 million.
- Together, the four companies accounted for $440 million, or about 69% of Nigeria’s $635 million in startup funding during the period.

#### **What you should know**
The pattern remained unchanged in 2025 with Nigerian startups [raising a total of $442.8 million in the year](https://nairametrics.com/2026/01/29/nigerias-most-funded-startups-capture-82-9-of-2025-capital-inflow/). With $635 million already raised in the first nine months of 2026, Nigerian startups have surpassed 2025 full-year record and are on course to top the African startup funding table this year.

web.title: Meet the founders behind Nigeria’s biggest startup funding ...
web.description:
[Close](https://nairametrics.com/2026/06/26/meet-the-founders-behind-nigerias-biggest-startup-funding-rounds-in-may/)

![Meet the founders behind Nigeria’s biggest startup funding rounds in May](https://media.nairametrics.com/2026/06/Image-2026-06-26T121847.065-1.jpg)

Nigeria’s startup ecosystem delivered one of its strongest funding performances of 2026 in May, attracting approximately $58.5 million across major deals involving fintech, logistics, Agritech, and enterprise technology companies.

According to startup funding data for May 2026, five Nigerian startups—LemFi, BFREE, MAX, Sycamore and Tomato Jos accounted for the bulk of Nigeria’s fundraising activity, approximately $57 million (97.4% of the funds raised in the country) during the month, while other ventures such as CashAfrica, Andela, and Pullus Africa also secured fresh capital of $500,000 each to support expansion efforts.

#### **5. Mira Mehta (Tomato Jos) – $2 million**
The new financing is expected to support processing capacity expansion and strengthen the company’s supply chain network.

#### **4. Babatunde Akin-Moses (Sycamore) – $5 million**
Babatunde Akin-Moses, co-founder and CEO of Sycamore, led the fintech company to a $5 million debt raise in May 2026.

Akin-Moses has positioned Sycamore as a trusted platform in Nigeria’s growing digital finance ecosystem, emphasizing responsible lending and financial inclusion. The latest funding is expected to support loan book expansion and strengthen the company’s investment offerings.

#### **1. Ridwan Olalere (LemFi) – $32 million**
At the top of the list is Ridwan Olalere, co-founder and CEO of LemFi, the cross-border payments startup that secured $32 million in a Series B extension round, making it the largest Nigerian startup raise in May 2026.

Olalere represents a growing class of Nigerian founders building globally competitive fintech companies from African roots.

The company has grown rapidly under Olalere’s leadership, serving more than two million users globally and processing over $1 billion in monthly transaction volume according to reports accompanying its May 2026 funding round. The latest funding round is expected to accelerate the company’s expansion strategy, strengthen its cross-border payments infrastructure, and support new financial products for immigrants and emerging market consumers.

#### **More insight**
- Malik Asamu, co-founder and CEO of CashAfrica, raised $500,000 in pre-seed funding, positioning the startup among Nigeria’s emerging fintech ventures.
- Carrol Chang, CEO of Andela, also featured among founders who secured funding in May 2026.

web.description:
[Close](https://nairametrics.com/2026/10/12/nigerian-startups-raise-11-3-million-in-september-2026-down-97-from-august/)

![Nigerian startups raise $11.3 million in September 2026, down 97% from August](https://cdn.nairametrics.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/start-up.webp)

Nigeria’s startup ecosystem recorded a sharp moderation in funding in September 2026, with nine startups attracting a combined $11.3 million, compared with $364.1 million raised by 20 startups in August.

#### **What the data is saying**
More startups received funding in September 2026 than in the corresponding month of 2025, yet the total capital mobilized was substantially lower.

#### **More Insight**
**Aeon,** a deeptech startup, raised $1 million in a pre-seed round from Terra Industries.

The transaction accounted for approximately 8.8% of September’s total funding.

- Notably, the investment represents a connection between two companies operating in the broader technology ecosystem: Terra Industries, which featured among Nigeria’s largest startup fundraisers in August, participated as an investor in Aeon’s September round.

- Two startups, Trade Lenda and AirSmat, each raised $200,000 through venture rounds backed by Village Capital.
